discovery: Discovery of superconductivity in organic molecular conductors

nominees.name: Denis Jérome
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire de Physique des Solides, CNRS / Université Paris-Saclay, France

subfield: Condensed matter physics: strongly correlated electrons and superconductivity
motivation: In 1980 Bechgaard designed and synthesised the (TMTSF)2X salts, and Jérome, applying hydrostatic pressure, found superconductivity in (TMTSF)2PF6. It was the first superconductor made from organic molecules. The discovery created a new class of materials whose soft, chemically tunable lattices let pressure, strain and disorder move electrons cleanly between superconductivity, spin-density waves, Mott insulators and quantum spin liquids. The Bechgaard salts and their two-dimensional BEDT-TTF descendants became model systems for central questions in correlated-electron physics: unconventional pairing beside antiferromagnetism, bandwidth-controlled Mott transitions, quasi-one-dimensional non-Fermi-liquid behaviour, field-induced spin-density waves and quantized Hall plateaus. Their phase diagrams anticipated the competition between magnetism and superconductivity later found in cuprates, iron pnictides and heavy fermions. This was a model collaboration between chemistry and physics, and it opened a field that is still producing new physics after forty-five years.
